newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Essar Cellphone targets 1 mln subscribers.
newsitem.headline: India's Essar Cellphone targets 1 mln subscribers.

text.p: Indian satellite communications company Essar Cellphone said on Wednesday that it expects its number of mobile phone subscribers to increase over the next five years to at least one million from 38,000.

"We hope to have over one million subscribers by the year 2002 and will take our share in north India to at least 60 percent," Essar Cellphone chairman Jan Erik Boers told a news conference in the Indian capital.

Essar Cellphone, a joint venture between India's Essar group and Swiss PTT, has been authorised to operate cellular networks in the states of Delhi, Rajasthan and Haryana, as well as the eastern section of Uttar Pradesh state.
Currently it operates only in Delhi, where its 46 percent share of the capital's cellular phone market translates into 38,000 subscribers.
"We will start providing services in the other three states later this year," Boers chairman said.
Boers said cellular phones had not yet taken off in India to the extent envisaged by the company.
"Some of the government policies, like a very high tariff rate and high duty on the import of handsets, were major deterrents," Boer said.
He said some 65 to 70 percent of the handsets were from the black market, undercutting Essar sales.
"Our plans are quite simply focussed on becoming north India's number one cellphone operator," Boer said.
India's Sterling Computers Ltd has a 51 percent stake in Essar Cellphone, Essar group chairman Shasi Ruia said.
Swiss PTT holds a 30 percent stake through Mobile West. CCII Mauritius owns 10 percent, and overseas companies hold the remaining nine percent
Ruia said Essar Cellphone plans to increase its equity base to eight billion rupees ($225 million) from the current level of 6.5 billion rupees ($185 million) within three years.

Once the equity capital is increased, Sterling Computers will retain a 51 percent stake. Swiss PTT's share will rise to 32.56 percent, CCII's share will fall to 8.65 percent and other foreign companies will hold 7.79 percent, he said.
Essar Cellphone said in a statement that Siemens AG had been selected as the suppliers of the network infrastructure for the three states where it plans to start operations.
